hunt.name: Akira Ransomware: GOST Tunneling and Data Impact
hunt.description: This hunt follows the Akira ransomware attack chain as observed by researchers, focusing on the post-compromise stages of persistence and impact. It identifies the deployment of the GOST (Go Simple Tunnel) utility, often disguised as a system process in the PerfLogs directory, and the subsequent execution of RClone for data exfiltration. The hunt then moves to the impact phase, looking for the characteristic PowerShell/WMI commands used to inhibit system recovery by deleting volume shadow copies, and finally identifies Akira ransomware artifacts including specific file hashes and log markers. By using a phased approach, the hunt allows an analyst to see the progression from a persistent tunnel to active data destruction.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (LOWER(file_path) LIKE 'c:\perflogs\%' OR instr(',' || '{{akira_hashes}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(file_hash_sha256) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')

config.expected_signal: A list of hostnames. Any result in C:\PerfLogs or matching report hashes is suspicious.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS proc, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%rclone%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%rclone%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY LOWER(process_name) HAVING hosts <= 3
config.description: Identify hosts where RClone is executing and determine if it is a rare occurrence in the environment.
config.expected_signal: A stack-count showing RClone is only on a few hosts. If it is not a standard IT tool, any hit is suspicious.
